As it follows from a result by Varnavides , this number is at least cp2 with some c = c( ) > 0, and Croot has recently shown that it is in fact cp2(1+o(1)) as p ! 1. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. A three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$ is an ordered triple $(x, x+d, x+2d) \in \mathbb{F}_p^3$ with $d \in \mathbb{F}_p$ (including the degenerate case $d=0$). For a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$, let $T(A)$ denote the number of three-term arithmetic progressions $(x, x+d, x+2d)$ with all three terms in $A$.

For a parameter $\alpha \in (0, 1/2)$, define
$$ m(\alpha, p) \;=\; \min igl\{\, T(A) \;:\; A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p,\ |A| = \lfloor \alpha p floor \, igr\}. $$
By a theorem of Varnavides, there exists $c(\alpha) > 0$ such that $m(\alpha, p) \ge c(\alpha)\, p^2$ for all sufficiently large primes $p$, and it is known that $m(\alpha, p) = c(\alpha)\, p^{2(1+o(1))}$ as $p 	o \infty$ for fixed $\alpha$.

(a) For the specific case $\alpha = 1/2$ (so $|A| = (p-1)/2$), determine the minimum possible value of $T(A)$ as a function of $p$.

(b) Determine the order of magnitude of the constant $c(\alpha)$ as $\alpha 	o 0^+$.

status_evidence.title: The Minimal Number of Three-Term Arithmetic Progressions Modulo a Prime Converges to a Limit
status_evidence.snippet: Croot proves N(t,p) converges to a limit as p → ∞, but does not determine its order in t.
status_evidence.claim: Croot established convergence of the minimal density but the order of magnitude of c(α) as α → 0 is not determined.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Additive Combinatorics (Croot–Lev)
status_evidence.snippet: It seems to be a difficult problem to determine the order of magnitude of the constant c(α) as α → 0.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open.

artifact.status_search_result: Croot (2008) proved that the normalized minimal count N(α,p) converges to a limit as p → ∞, establishing the p^{2(1+o(1))} asymptotic. However, determining the order of magnitude of the limiting constant c(α) as α → 0 remains open; no recent results indicate this has been resolved.
